title: Dashboard (home) — flow inspiration
intro: Product-first flow gallery for the Essentials 2.0 dashboard: the first screen after login, which has to answer per role what's happening, what needs me and whether everything is working, then get people into the right module in one click. Scope: role-based homes, today's agenda, center/room overview, system health, a few precise KPIs, action items, customizable widgets, module navigation and the first-run setup guide. The full live room wall (Recording), the calendar (Scheduling) and full reports (Reports) are covered in their own galleries. Sources: Mobbin (all flows shown) and Refero (searched, but its image server refused every step image, so no Refero flow is included). Research date: 2026-09-30.
baseline: Today's LS Essentials dashboard is a set of module tiles (Recording, Video Review, Reports, Scenario management, Calendar) plus a Center Overview of rooms and their calendar activity; the team itself calls it weak. The LearningSpace Enterprise facelift (mid-2026) was an accessibility and visual cleanup, redrawn not rewritten: modules in their own row, a raised Upcoming tab, a Your Activities tab, buttons instead of links, responsive to iPad and mobile, with a role-specific widget layer deferred to phase 2. Essentials 2.0 aims for a central dashboard that combines learner feedback, faculty grading and reports, a system-health status fed by the automatic per-room device check, and a fast multi-room center overview, under the rule that a good dashboard shows little, but precisely. Whether to build it new or facelift the existing one is still open.

jobs.title: Role-based home
jobs.description: Different first screens per role (admin vs. faculty vs. tech vs. learner), switching roles/views, what's hidden vs. shown per role

jobs.title: Today & upcoming
jobs.description: Today's agenda (sessions by time and room), "up next", countdowns, jumping straight into the session's action (start recording, open checklist, open debrief)

jobs.title: Center overview / room status
jobs.description: Compact multi-room status (free / in use / recording / problem) on the home, drill into one room. The full live wall belongs to Recording.

jobs.title: System health at a glance
jobs.description: "All systems OK" vs. warning vs. failing, last self-test result, what's broken and the guided path to fix it or who to call

jobs.title: Few, precise KPIs
jobs.description: A handful of metrics (utilisation, sessions run, recordings, learner contact hours), trend vs. last period, click-through to the full report

jobs.title: Action items & notifications
jobs.description: What needs me: pending grading, checklists to review, recordings to share, setup tasks, approvals. Inbox vs. cards; dismiss / snooze / done

jobs.title: Customizable widgets
jobs.description: Add / remove / reorder / resize widgets, widget library, defaults per role, reset to default. Also counter-examples of clutter.

jobs.title: Module navigation & quick actions
jobs.description: How the home exposes modules (tiles vs. sidebar vs. command palette), global search, quick-create ("new session", "new scenario"), recents / favourites

jobs.title: Empty state & setup guide
jobs.description: A brand-new center: setup checklist (rooms, cameras, users, first course), progress, sample data, "what's new" announcements for existing users

products.name: Fresha
products.why: The closest match to a sim coordinator's day: a home with two sales KPIs and a 7-day trend above today's next appointments (time, status, staff), plus a staff-as-columns day grid with a now line that reads like rooms-as-columns. Its agenda rows show status only, with no Start action.

products.name: Better Stack
products.why: The failing state done properly: an Ongoing incident and a sidebar count on the home, then Escalate (naming who was paged), Acknowledge (stamping the owner) and Resolve with a timeline. It shows no 'all OK' summary at all.

products.name: Google Home
products.why: Devices grouped under room headers, with Offline shown on the tile itself so a problem room is visible without drilling in. Its fix path is a generic help list plus Contact us, which is the weak version to improve on.

products.name: Patreon
products.why: The clearest role variant: the identity switcher keeps the current role in the sidebar footer, and switching rebuilds the home and cuts the sidebar from ten management modules with Create to five discovery items without it. The creator home keeps one KPI with a Go to Insights link.

products.name: Aboard
products.why: An admin home (quick-create pills, an approvals card with '1 unhandled') and an employee home (onboarding banner, personal task and profile chips) in one product. The switch is a one-way link with no role label on the far side.

products.name: Square
products.why: The same product shows both sides of 'little but precise': a lean Key Metrics row with vs-prior pills (N/A when there is no history) and one location/date scope, and a fuller Performance home that tips into clutter.

products.name: Shopify
products.why: A setup guide that is the home (N of M, one expanded task with its own CTA), stays as a side rail while you do the task in the module, offers sample data, and leaves with Dismiss guide and 'All caught up'.

products.name: Linear
products.why: Inbox semantics made explicit: Done, Snooze, Mark all as read and Delete all are separate actions, the badge counts unread only, and snoozed items stay visible after the unread count hits zero.

products.name: Notion
products.why: A calm fixed home instead of tiles: recents, Upcoming events grouped by day above My tasks with checkboxes, honest empty sections, and a sidebar with Home, Search, Inbox and New. First-run is a live checklist page, not a modal tour.

products.name: Rivian
products.why: One status dominates the home (battery %) with one primary action pair under it (Lock/Unlock), then small status widgets with one-tap actions, and a coloured Updates card as the only action item.

products.name: Jira
products.why: The full widget machinery leadership asks for: a 31-gadget library, per-dashboard viewers/editors and per-gadget chrome. Its useful part is small: an admin-set Default dashboard that 'affects all users', layout presets and an Assigned to Me card.

products.name: Google Analytics
products.why: Counter-example: a home of equal-weight KPI tabs, realtime and suggested-metric cards, each with its own controls, and no single answer about where to look first or what 'OK' means.

patterns.title: Health is shown on the list; the fix has an owner
patterns.body: Google Home puts Offline on the room's device tile, so a problem is visible without drilling in. Better Stack goes further: the home leads with the Ongoing incident and a sidebar count, Escalate names who was paged, Acknowledge stamps an owner and Resolve closes it with a timeline. Google Home's fix path is only a help-article list plus Contact us. For Essentials, a failed room self-test should appear on the room in the overview and become an owned item (sim tech acknowledges, resolves or escalates), handing off to Recording for the device check.

patterns.title: One dominant status, one primary action
patterns.body: Rivian's home is dominated by one number with one action pair under it, and everything else is smaller. Google Analytics is the opposite: many equal cards, each with its own controls, and no single answer. The dashboard's first line should be one verdict ('All rooms ready' or '2 rooms need attention') with one action, not a row of peer widgets.

patterns.title: A few KPIs with a vs-prior pill; depth lives in Reports
patterns.body: Square's lean home shows five metrics, each with a 'vs prior weekday' pill that says N/A when there is no history, under one location/date scope, with Reports in the sidebar. Fresha pairs two sales numbers with a 7-day trend; Patreon keeps one KPI with 'Go to Insights'. Square's own fuller home (nine metrics, banking promos, a near-empty chart) shows where it tips over. Three or four center KPIs with a period delta and a click-through to Reports is the evidence-backed ceiling.

patterns.title: Role homes are different jobs, and the current role is always named
patterns.body: Patreon's switch rebuilds the whole home: the creator sidebar has management modules and Create, the member sidebar has five discovery items and no Create, and the active role stays in the sidebar footer with a checkmark in the switcher. Aboard's admin home carries quick-create and approvals while the employee home carries personal onboarding, but its switch is a one-way link with no role label afterwards. Coordinator, faculty and learner homes should differ in content, not just hide menu items, and always show which role you are in.

patterns.title: Today is a short list by time, above the tasks
patterns.body: Fresha lists today's next appointments with time, status (Booked/Started), staff and duration; Notion groups Upcoming by day above My tasks, so the agenda and the to-dos share one scroll without a full calendar. Fresha's day grid uses staff as columns with a now line, which maps to rooms as columns. Neither puts the item's action on the row: Fresha shows status only, so 'Start recording' or 'Open debrief' on the agenda item has no reference here.

patterns.title: Action items: done, snooze and read are different, and the count is precise
patterns.body: Linear separates Done, Snooze, Mark all as read and Delete all, counts unread only, and keeps snoozed items listed after the unread count reaches zero. Shopify and Aboard surface countable work as one card ('2 orders to fulfill', '1 unhandled' time-off request) rather than a feed. Pending grading, recordings to share and checklists to review fit this model, and each item opens Debrief, Recording or Courses directly.

patterns.title: The setup guide lives on the home, follows you into the module, then leaves
patterns.body: Shopify's guide is the home for a new store (N of M, one expanded task with its own button), stays as a right rail while you do the task in the product editor, offers a sample product, and leaves via Dismiss guide and 'All caught up'. Fresha keeps setup progress in the header instead of taking the page. Better Stack shows the cost of not leaving: its checklist takes half the home while an incident is ongoing. A new center's checklist (rooms, cameras, users, first course) should hand off into Inventory, User management and Courses, then get out of the way.

patterns.title: Admin-set defaults beat end-user widget building
patterns.body: Jira's most useful piece is the Default dashboard that 'affects all users', with five layout presets; its 31-gadget library, per-dashboard viewers/editors and per-gadget chrome are too much for non-technical faculty. Google Home keeps customisation to Reorder and Edit on Favourites. For the phase-2 widget layer, this points to per-role defaults set by the coordinator plus light show/hide or reorder, not a library.

open_questions: No product puts the item's action on the today row. Fresha's agenda shows status only (mobbin:3c0845a8-624f-4a47-ad80-e57ab4bb1531), so 'Start recording', 'Open checklist' or 'Open debrief' from the session row has to be designed without a reference. The same goes for linking the two signals: what does the today row show when that session's room has failed its self-test?

Multi-room overview is still a gap. The nearest evidence is Google Home's room-grouped device tiles (mobbin:8b62ccef-2298-47f2-8193-d740fac356e4), Fresha's staff columns (mobbin:7df9c1e2-cfd5-4c9f-84eb-718683ff8ed3) and Square's locations table (mobbin:066793dc-d7b2-44ca-ab1b-7e67da3dbe78). No flow shows a free / in use / recording / problem strip for rooms. Security and room-booking apps (UniFi, Verkada, Robin, Skedda) returned nothing usable again, and Refero was unusable (HTTP 403 on every step image).

What does 'all OK' look like? Better Stack shows health only through the presence of incidents (mobbin:ed948f6a-ac7b-4742-add9-fafc58fda138), and Rivian shows one metric (mobbin:7b9d5db3-24d8-49ae-827e-218db2b446dc). Should the dashboard show a green verdict with the last self-test time, or nothing until something fails? And who owns a failing room: is there a sim tech on duty to acknowledge it, as in Better Stack (mobbin:fc2ba92b-4783-43da-92c7-8acf4f16a080)?

Role switching versus a merged home. Patreon switches identities (mobbin:63dda702-ffb9-4b29-a69e-a58be8bf9ad9) and Aboard jumps one way to an employee portal (mobbin:6ec8698e-d2a3-4d6f-a711-3e4025e51a71). In a sim center one person is often both coordinator and faculty. Is that a switcher, or one home with both sets of sections? And does the learner need a dashboard at all, or only Patreon's member-style lightweight page with their own recordings and feedback?

Build new versus facelift. The sections with the strongest evidence (a today list fed by Scheduling, health on the rooms, an inbox with done/snooze, a first-run guide) are data-driven and new; the existing module tiles map to a short sidebar (Patreon, Notion). Can the LS Enterprise facelift shell host these sections, or is the tile row itself what has to go?

Multi-campus is only a pointer: Square's location filter (mobbin:c0741e77-ac72-4f67-9b29-7a673ae0b0a3) and Google Home's home switcher (mobbin:8b62ccef-2298-47f2-8193-d740fac356e4) switch one scope at a time and say nothing about access across separate LS instances.
